Y our Annual Plan 2023: Financial Resilience Edition Why is an annual plan important? If you’ve seen your business through to the other side of the pandemic, you’re a survivor—and like every business that’s weathered the storm for over two years, you’ve shown signs of one trait that’s key to a company’s long-term success: resilience. There’s little doubt 2023 has more tests in store for business owners. And while there’s no knowing what those tests may be, there’s one thing that will also safeguard your company more than anything else: having an annual plan that’s designed through the lens of becoming more financially resilient. Put simply , an annual plan is the bridge between the vision you set for your business and the actual work it’ll take to move your business toward that vision. But often, annual planning is a rote, static exercise that—if it’s done at all—results in a document that gathers dust in a file cabinet. Y ou’re about to discover a new kind of annual plan—one that actually serves you and the health, growth and security of your company . It works because it starts with your passion and gives you the tools to translate that passion into specific actions. This annual plan will also grow and evolve with your business. It’ll allow you to adapt to sudden changes such as a loss in a revenue stream or supply issues, helping you learn and improve your process along the way . Creating a successful annual plan that boosts the financial resilience of your business relies on two things: clearly seeing how each business system is tied to financial health and effectively translating each of your goals in clear projects and tasks. If you can do both these things, you’ll head into 2023 with a solid yet flexible roadmap for success, whatever comes your way . This workbook will help you: • Understand the importance of creating an annual plan. • Assess the current performance of your business so you know where to focus. • Develop clear next steps to achieve your 2023 goals and routinely check in to make sure you’re on the right track. Steps to create your annual plan The fourth quarter of every year is the right time to start an annual plan. The challenges and accomplishments of the year you’re finishing up are fresh, and you avoid the trap of treating your annual plan like a New Y ear’s Resolution with all its good intentions and predictable failures. Set your intention to put meaningful time and thought into where you are now and how you want to build on that in the next year . Step 1: Imagine what it would be like to have real financial resilience Step 2: Assess the current state of your business Step 3: Prioritize your goals Step 4: Create quarterly milestones and monthly actions to lead you toward your annual goals Step 5: Empower your team to track and own results Step 6: Document your process and be prepared to adapt to the unexpected

Y our Annual Plan 2023: Financial Resilience Edition ASSESS THE CURRENT STATE OF YOUR BUSINESS One of the most important steps in creating an annual plan that’s anchored in building financial resilence is to take an honest look at the current state of your business. Y ou can’t achieve your goals and key targets on top of ineffective or broken systems. Keep this in mind as you answer the following questions to assess how each of your Seven Essential Systems currently supports the financial health of your business. For this exercise, answer each item honestly and objectively so you have a clear and truthful understanding of where you and your business stand now. This will uncover opportunities for where to improve your current systems so they more strongly impact financial growth. LEADERSHIP On a scale of 1 to 10 (with 1 being least positive, 10 being most positive), how would you rate your current leadership abilities? Why did you choose this score? What do you think would make it a 10? Are you in touch with your values and company vision to ensure you create a business that’s personally satisfying, financially stable and reflective of your needs and aspirations? Have you communicated your company’s future direction—along with your standards, expectations and measures for financial performance—to your employees in a way that challenges and inspires them to perform? Have you established the systems and structures that allow employees to be the most effective they can be? Do you communicate clearly and directly , even in difficult situations?

Y our Annual Plan 2023: Financial Resilience Edition DOCUMENT YOUR PROCESS AND BE PREPARED TO ADAPT TO THE UNEXPECTED One of the most effective (yet often neglected) ways to make sure your annual plan allows you to adapt to unexpected change is to look at the assumptions involved in creating it and consider any contingencies you may need to put in place. This worksheet will help you do that. It may also be useful to make copies of this document before you begin. In the columns below, list the assumptions you’ve used in this planning process. In other words, what have you taken for granted? That your team will stay the same? That your business will continue to grow at its current pace organically? Once you’ve identified those assumptions, list the parts of your business plan that are affected by each assumption and the indicators to watch over time—these will tell you if your assumptions are correct. Then, select the date when you’ll review those indicators to see if your assumptions are on track. At the time of your review, determine whether or not you need to reassess those portions of your business plan. If you do want to change your plan at that time, use the worksheet in the previous step to identify each item that needs to be adjusted, who will be accountable for revising it and when it’s due.
